author: Chris Vetter
title: Eau Claire County sues 3M, other PFAS makers, in Chippewa County Court - NewsBreak
text:
By Chris Vetter ,
6 hours ago
CHIPPEWA FALLS — Eau Claire County has filed a lawsuit against 3M Company, Chemguard Inc., The Chemours Company, Dupont De Nemours, and several other defendants “to recover any and all damages associated with the contamination of its airport with toxic chemicals known as PFAS.”
The case was filed last week in Chippewa County Court against a total of 20 defendants. The case has not yet been assigned to a judge, and no court dates have been set. Milwaukee-based Attolles Law Firm is representing the county.
The county is seeking an unspecified amount in punitive damages, plus compensatory damages to the property, along with attorney fees.
The 34-page lawsuit notes that the Chippewa Valley Regional Airport property, located at 3800 Starr Avenue, is owned by Eau Claire County, and it states that the land is “contaminated with PFAS chemicals.”
“At various times from the 1960s through today, defendants designed, manufactured, formulated, marketed, distributed and/or sold PFAS (including PFOA, PFOS, and the chemical precursors of PFOA and/or PFOS) and fluorosurfactant products including aqueous film-forming foam (AFFM), a fire-fighting agent used to control and extinguish Class B fuel fires,” the lawsuit reads.
The lawsuit claims those chemicals have been “released, used, stored and/or disposal of at or near (the airport), which allowed PFOS, PFOA and/or their chemical precursors to enter the environment and migrate through soil, groundwater, surface water, and stormwater, thereby contaminating plaintiff’s property.”
The county contends that the defendants “failed to disclose the toxic nature and harmful effects of these fluorosurfactant products or their wastes.”
The lawsuit notes that Eau Claire County is not part of a group of other municipalities in a settlement proposal with these companies. The county also is not seeking damages for contamination to the public drinking water system.
The lawsuit was filed in Chippewa County Court “because a substantial part of the events and omissions giving rise to plaintiff’s causes of action occurred in Chippewa County, and because the property and resources affected by defendants’ conduct are in Chippewa County.”
PFAS are “stable, man-made chemicals. They are highly water soluble, persistent in the environment and resistant to biological, environmental, or photochemical degradation,” the lawsuit reads. “Because these compounds are water-soluble and do not readily absorb to sediments or soil, they tend to stay in the water column and can be transported long distances.”
The lawsuit lists research done on PFAS and states that the defendants were aware of the chemicals’ hazards if consumed by humans.
“Defendants had a duty to evaluate and test such products adequately and thoroughly to determine their environmental fate and transport characteristics and potential human health and environmental impacts before they sold such products, but they breached this duty,” the lawsuit contends.
The city of Eau Claire filed a similar lawsuit in August 2023.
summary: CHIPPEWA FALLS — Eau Claire County has filed a lawsuit against 3M Company, Chemguard Inc., The Chemours Company, Dupont De Nemours, and several other defendants “to recover any and all damages associated with the contamination of its airport with toxic chemicals known as PFAS.” The case was filed last week in Chippewa County Court against a total of 20 defendants.
